messages:
zoe: dropped a new compact preview mock + a couple interaction options. two things I'm worried about: preview density on small screens and the verbosity of screen-reader announcements when bulk-pausing channels.

paul: nice frames. question: do we show full timeline (start/end) for a paused window or use a single duration chip like '1h' / 'until 3pm'? chips would keep rows tidy.

rita: chips feel good visually. but we need an explicit detail view on hover/focus that says timezone-aware times (e.g., 'paused until 15:00 PDT'). accessibility needs the timezone text included in the aria label.

nate: for density on narrow displays, we can collapse the preview into a single-line summary per channel: icon, truncated name, state chip, chevron to expand. expands in-place on tap/enter. keeps vertical rhythm.

marie: copy note: current mock uses "Bulk pause" and "Pause until". Research favors verbs users know — prefer "Pause notifications" and the chip label as "1 hour" or "Until 3pm". Avoid jargon like "suppress" in primary CTAs.

zoe: good — I'll swap to "Pause notifications" primary. also prototyped an "announce verbosity" control in the settings: brief vs detailed. Brief: only summary announcement ("2 channels paused"). Detailed: list each channel paused. ops-bot what do we think?

ops-bot: Accessibility rule: avoid firing a live announcement per item in bulk actions. Default to "brief" announcements. Provide a user setting for "detailed announcements" under accessibility preferences for power users.

paul: implementation: summary region with role=region and aria-live=polite. On bulk pause, set innerText to concise string like "Notifications paused for 3 channels". If user has detailed verbosity enabled, enqueue additional announcements but rate-limit to avoid flood.

rita: microcopy tweak: tooltip for chips should read: "Paused until 15:00 PDT (2h)" and the aria-describedby should reference that tooltip so screen readers get the exact end time. Also ensure the chip has aria-roledescription="pause chip" for clarity.

nate: keyboard: when expanding a row inline, move focus into the expanded panel and trap only within that panel until user closes it (Esc returns to row). This prevents disorienting tab jumps.

marie: mobile: instead of inline expansion, navigate to a single-channel detail sheet to preserve performance. keep the same aria semantics and announce navigation with a polite live region like "Opening Email pause details".

zoe: performance note: lazy-render expanded details; avoid rendering long channel lists unless user expands or taps "show all". reduces DOM pressure for large orgs.

paul: UX question: do we keep a small confirmation snackbar after pause actions or inline toast near the header? snackbar with undo seems fine: "Paused 3 channels — Undo". but undo should be accessible via keyboard (focusable) and have aria-live assertive? maybe polite is safer.

ops-bot: Use polite aria-live for success messages to avoid interrupting AT. If immediate corrective action is needed, use assertive sparingly. For Undo, make the action focusable and include an accessible name like "Undo pause for 3 channels".

rita: design decision: show iconography next to chips (pause icon) for visual scanning. pair icon with accessible label; never rely on color alone.

nate: dev note: summary header should expose a data attribute with counts for analytics, but don't duplicate that into the live announcement text. keep announcement human-friendly.

marie: small accessibility polish: when a single-channel pause expires, announce "Notifications resumed for Email" once. don't spam when multiple expirations happen simultaneously; group by 5s window.

zoe: OK actionable list for next iteration: 1) swap primary microcopy to "Pause notifications" and chips for durations; 2) add announce-verbosity toggle (default brief); 3) summary polite live region + optional detailed announcements behind setting; 4) accessible tooltips for chips with TZ; 5) mobile navigates to detail sheet; 6) snackbar with focusable undo, polite live. I'll push updated frames and a short prototype of the live-string changes. ETA EOD. Thanks! :seedling:
